docs.title: AGENTS.md for your game
docs.description: A ready-made AGENTS.md template for your game repository that helps AI coding agents integrate Open Play correctly, and how to use it together with the MCP server.
docs.body:
# AGENTS.md for your game

`AGENTS.md` is the rules file that AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and similar) read automatically from the root of your repository. When agents connect a game to Open Play, the mistakes they make most often are: guessing an endpoint or header, putting the server key in the client, skipping the CSRF and session rules, not pinning the plugin schema, removing a domain too early, and leaving stale cached JavaScript running in production. The template on this page puts the rules that prevent those mistakes into one file. The rules come from problems met in real game integrations (the example games ArenaRace and LanternTide), and every rule links to the docs page behind it.

## How to use it

1. Download the template: [`https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/AGENTS.md`](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/AGENTS.md) (or copy the block below) and save it as `AGENTS.md` in the root of **your game repository**. If you already have an `AGENTS.md`, add the template under an "Open Play integration" heading.
2. In "Project facts", replace the placeholders `<YOUR_DEV_ENV_ID>`, `<YOUR_PROD_ENV_ID>`, `<OPEN_PLAY_BASE_URL>`, `<DEV_GAME_ORIGIN>`, `<PROD_GAME_ORIGIN>` and `<SDK_VERSION>` with your values. Environment ids are not secret; **do not write keys or secrets into the file**.
3. Add the Open Play MCP server to your agent ([Using AI tools](ai-tools.md)): `claude mcp add --transport http open-play https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/mcp`. The template tells the agent to use `search_docs`, `read_doc`, `search_sdk` and `get_sdk_symbol` first, so it takes behavior from the current docs and not from memory.
4. Delete the sections your game does not use (for example section 6 if you use no plugins). Add your own rules (code style, test commands, branch workflow) above or below the template.

## What the template covers

| Section | What it prevents |
|---|---|
| MCP first | Endpoints, headers and field names written from guesses |
| Keys and environments | A server key leaking into the client, dev and prod mixed up |
| Sign-in and sessions | Guest flow, Google popup with a redirect fallback, the redirect base (`/auth/callback`), the CSRF race, single active session, account deletion |
| Domains and browser | Unregistered origins, removing a live domain too early, a proxy dropping headers |
| Player data | A separate save server, writing without `If-Match` |
| Plugins | Schema mismatch, a command resent with a new key, a disabled grant after a version bump |
| Realtime | Ticket reuse, replayed inputs, a one-at-a-time input flow that feels laggy |
| Caching and deploys | A CDN overriding `no-cache` and keeping old JavaScript |
| Errors and limits | Parsing error text, a shared per-IP bucket |
| Testing and Do / Don't | A checklist before you say "done" |

The template is in English because AI tools and the MCP index of the docs site work best with English text. It is also listed in the "Optional" section of the `https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/llms.txt` index.

> [!NOTE]
> The template is a **rules file**, not a guarantee from Open Play. The docs pages are the only source of truth for behavior; if the template and a page disagree, the page is right. We recommend trying the template in a real agent session and tightening it for your game.

## The full template

````markdown
# AGENTS.md — integrating this game with Open Play

> Drop this file in the root of your game repository. Replace every `<PLACEHOLDER>` and delete rules that do not apply.
> Source and updates: https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/AGENTS.md

This game uses **Open Play**, a game backend platform: player identity and sessions, player data (cloud save), characters, economy, store, rewards, social features, leaderboards, notifications, plugins and realtime connections. The game talks to Open Play over HTTP and WebSocket, through the TypeScript SDK (`@ferdiunal/open-play-ts`) or the Unity SDK. The game does **not** run its own account or save server for anything Open Play provides.

Docs root: https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/ — every rule below links to its page.

## 0. Project facts (fill in)

- Environment ids (the `x-crx-env` value): dev `<YOUR_DEV_ENV_ID>`, prod `<YOUR_PROD_ENV_ID>`. One environment per stage; data is never shared between them.
- Open Play base URL: `<OPEN_PLAY_BASE_URL>` (the API address the browser calls).
- Game origins registered per environment: `<DEV_GAME_ORIGIN>`, `<PROD_GAME_ORIGIN>`.
- SDK version (exact, no `^`, no `latest`): `<SDK_VERSION>`.

## 1. Use the Open Play MCP server first

Before you write any call to Open Play, **look it up**. Never guess an endpoint, header, field or error code.

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http open-play https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/mcp
```

Cursor (`.cursor/mcp.json`) and VS Code (`.vscode/mcp.json`, key `servers`): `{"mcpServers":{"open-play":{"url":"https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/mcp"}}}`.

- `search_docs` then `read_doc` (for example `auth/oauth`) for behavior and HTTP contracts.
- `search_sdk` then `get_sdk_symbol` (for example `PlayerSession`, `sdk: "typescript"` or `"unity"`) for exact SDK signatures.
- The server is read-only and public; it never needs or sees a key. If the docs and your memory disagree, the docs win.
- No MCP available: read https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/llms.txt (index) or `llms-full.txt` (everything).

Docs: [Using AI tools (MCP)](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/getting-started/ai-tools.html).

## 2. Keys and environments

- **Client** code (browser, WebGL, mobile) knows only the environment id and the player session. It carries **no secret**.
- A **server key** (`crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>`) lives only on your own server or backend-for-frontend (BFF): in its secret store, never in the client bundle, the repository, logs, or `.env` files that are committed. Use a separate key per environment and service, with an expiry.
- A client key is not a server key; calling a server endpoint with it is rejected. Player operations use the player session, not a key.
- Never point a dev build at the prod environment or the reverse. Read the environment id from per-stage configuration.
- Do not hard-code or print secrets, tokens, cookies or `x-csrf-token` values in code, tests, logs or analytics.

Docs: [Security](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/operations/security.html), [API keys](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/panel/game-settings-api-keys.html), [Production checklist](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/operations/production-checklist.html).

## 3. Sign-in and sessions

- **Guest first.** Open a guest session on first launch so the player plays at once; offer Google (or email) later and **link** it to the same player. Linking a guest upgrades the same player id; progress is kept.
- **Google OAuth:** try a popup window and fall back to a full-page redirect when the popup is blocked. Open the popup synchronously inside the click handler, before any `await`. Let the callback page hand the result back (for example through `BroadcastChannel`) and close itself. Pattern with a tested example: [Google sign-in in a popup](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/auth/oauth-popup.html).
- The server builds the Google `redirect_uri` from the configured **redirect base + `/google`**. The base must end at `/auth/callback` (not `/google`); the redirect URI registered with Google must be exactly `<base>/google`, and that path must be a page of your game that finishes the sign-in.
- The OAuth `code` and `state` are single-use: finish exactly once, then remove them from the address bar (`history.replaceState`). Use the SDK helpers; they bind `state` to the browser tab.
- A cookie session sends `x-crx-env` on every call and a CSRF token on every state-changing request. The token is **single-use and rotates**: never send two mutations at once with the same token, and keep the new token from each response. The SDKs serialize this for you; share the token between tabs with the SDK `csrf.channel` option. Retry a CSRF `403` once with a fresh token.
- Session lifetime is 30 days sliding, 180 days absolute. On `401` refresh or sign in again; do not loop.
- If the environment allows a **single active session**, a newer sign-in revokes the older one. Handle `reauthRequired` with a clear "signed in on another device" screen and a sign-in button, not a silent retry.
- Show the sign-in methods you actually enabled; hide the rest. Do not use SDK methods the docs mark as unsupported.
- **Account deletion** is a store requirement (Apple, Google Play): provide an in-game "Delete my account" action (`POST /v1/auth/account/delete`, `confirm: "delete_my_account"`). A linked account must have signed in within the last 10 minutes (`recent_sign_in_required`): ask the player to sign in again, then repeat.
- Verify identity on your own game server with the access JWT and the JWKS, never by trusting a client-sent player id.

Docs: [Auth overview](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/auth/overview.html), [Guest](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/auth/guest.html), [Google sign-in](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/auth/oauth.html), [Sessions and CSRF](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/auth/sessions-and-csrf.html), [Account linking](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/auth/account-linking.html), [Account deletion](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/auth/account-deletion.html), [Server-side verification](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/auth/server-verification.html).

## 4. Domains and calling from the browser

- Register **every origin your game runs on** in each environment's domain list (Game settings, Environments and domains): one full domain per line, no wildcards, no ports, at most 10, and a domain belongs to one environment only. An unregistered origin gets `403` on writes.
- Call Open Play either directly (your game domain is in the list; the server sends CORS headers with credentials) or through a same-origin reverse proxy that forwards `Cookie`, `Origin`, `x-crx-env`, `x-csrf-token`, `Idempotency-Key`, `If-Match` and the WebSocket upgrade, and that forwards the real client IP.
- **Moving to a new domain:** add the new domain and the new OAuth redirect first, test it, and only then retire the old one. **Removing a domain from an environment locks that live host out immediately.** Guest identities are per-origin: a new domain starts new guests.
- Send `Origin` only as the browser sets it. Never fake it in game code.

Docs: [Architecture and hosting](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/getting-started/architecture-and-hosting.html), [Environments and domains](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/panel/game-settings-environments.html).

## 5. Player data (cloud save)

- Use the generic per-player key-value store; **do not build a game-specific save server**. The value is an opaque JSON object the server never interprets; your game owns the format and its version field.
- Limits: key `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`, at most 16 keys per player, 64 KiB per value, 60 writes per minute per player. Store large integers as strings.
- **There is no blind write.** Every `PUT` sends exactly one of `If-None-Match: *` (create) or `If-Match: "<version>"` (update). On `409 version_conflict` read the remote record, merge it with your own rule, retry. `428` means a precondition header is missing.
- Batch saves (on level end, on pause, on a timer), not every frame. Keep a local copy and reconcile on sign-in; a guest-to-Google link keeps the same player.
- Never write personal data you do not need. Player data is erased with the account.

Docs: [Player data](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/guides/player-data.html), [Idempotency and concurrency](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/reference/idempotency-and-concurrency.html).

## 6. Plugins (game-specific server logic)

- Call plugins only through **generated bindings**, never hand-written DTOs or copied field names. Get the schema document from `GET /v1/plugins/<PLUGIN_ID>/schema` and generate bindings from it.
- **Pin** `pluginId`, `schemaSha256`, `protocolVersion`, `codecProfile` and the plugin version in your release manifest. A mismatch must **fail closed**: show an "update the game" screen, never talk to the server with the wrong fields. After every server update compare the live digest with the pin (at startup or in CI).
- Every command carries an `Idempotency-Key`, generated **once** per logical action and reused on retries. If the outcome is uncertain (timeout, drop), resend with the **same key and body** or ask the result query; never generate a new key for the same action.
- Retry only when it is safe: idempotent calls on network errors, `429`, `503`, with exponential backoff and jitter, and honor `Retry-After`. Never retry business rejections (`422`).
- `int64` values travel as decimal strings. Send `If-Match` / `expectedVersion` when writing a shared resource; on `409` re-read first.
- If a plugin call suddenly returns `403`, check that the plugin is **enabled for that environment** and that the enabled version matches the server version. A server version bump needs its grant switched too.

Docs: [Plugins overview](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/plugins/overview.html), [Bindings and pinning](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/plugins/bindings.html), [Calling plugins](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/plugins/calling-plugins.html).

## 7. Realtime

- Use the SDK realtime client; if you implement the protocol yourself follow it exactly (single-use ticket, `Origin`, subprotocol).
- Ask for a **new ticket on every connection**. On a drop reconnect with exponential backoff, `Join` again with the last cursor (durable streams) or without one (ephemeral state), and on `ResyncRequired` drop the cursor and join fresh.
- Unacknowledged inputs are **not replayed**; continue from the latest snapshot. Pipeline inputs inside the SDK window (default 4 in flight); one input per round trip makes fast games feel laggy on real networks.
- Keep the frame rate below 40 per second; at most 4 sockets per player. Handle idle close (`4100`) with a "Continue" screen. An open socket does not keep the session alive.
- Notification and chat sockets cannot be opened straight from a browser; use inbox polling or REST.

Docs: [Realtime overview](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/realtime/overview.html), [Protocol](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/realtime/protocol.html), [Reconnect and limits](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/realtime/reconnect-and-limits.html).

## 8. Caching and deploys

- Serve your game's JavaScript modules and config (including the file that holds the environment id) with `Cache-Control: no-cache`, or content-hash the filenames. A stale config file after a deploy silently runs the old integration.
- If a CDN sits in front, set it to **respect existing headers** for HTML, JS and CSS. A CDN default browser TTL can override your `no-cache` and keep old code for hours.
- Never put a CDN cache in front of API responses that carry a cookie or `Authorization`.
- Deploy order when Open Play changes a plugin: new server and grant, then client with regenerated bindings. Pin the SDK version exactly and upgrade from the changelog.

Docs: [Production checklist](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/operations/production-checklist.html), [Versioning](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/reference/versioning.html).

## 9. Errors and rate limits

- Core endpoints return **plain-text** errors; plugin endpoints return a JSON envelope (`code`, `message`, `retryable`, `requestId`). Decide by status code and JSON `code`, **never by parsing message text**. Log `requestId` / `x-request-id`.
- There is no general per-key quota, but identity endpoints are limited per client IP (for example 30 guest sign-ins per minute). Behind a proxy or a shared network (NAT, a hosting platform's shared egress) many players share one IP: forward the real client IP.
- Back off on `429`, `503` and network errors; wait `Retry-After` when present. Never loop on `401`, `403` or `422`.

Docs: [Errors](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/reference/errors.html), [Rate limits](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/reference/rate-limits.html).

## 10. Testing checklist (before you call it done)

1. Fresh browser profile: guest sign-in, play, reload, same player and progress.
2. Guest upgraded to Google keeps progress; a second browser signs in to the same account and loads the save.
3. Two tabs open: no CSRF `403` storm; sign-out in one tab is handled in the other.
4. Same command sent twice with the same `Idempotency-Key` gives one effect.
5. Two devices write the same player-data key: the `409` is merged, nothing is lost.
6. Kill the network mid-command and mid-socket: the game recovers without duplicate effects.
7. Prod build points at the prod environment id and prod origin; dev at dev. No secrets in the bundle (search it).
8. Run these in a **headless browser or test harness** you control; do not test against another team's environment or real player data.

## 11. Unity (only if this game is built with Unity)

- Use the `com.openplay.sdk` C# package, not hand-written HTTP. It has guest and email/password sign-in, plugin commands and the realtime socket; it has **no** Google OAuth helper.
- **Native builds** send a fixed `Origin` (derived from `BaseUrl`, overridable with `NativeOrigin`). That origin must be in the environment's domain list or the global allowed list, otherwise ticket and WebSocket requests get `403`.
- **WebGL** uses the browser's cookies and WebSocket. The game page and `BaseUrl` must be the **same origin** (`webgl_cross_origin_unsupported` otherwise); serve both through one host or a same-origin reverse proxy. Do not set `Cookie` or `Origin` yourself.
- Pin plugin schemas on startup: call `PluginClient.VerifyServerSchemaAsync()` and stop with a clear message on a mismatch instead of sending commands to a changed server.
- Only Unity 6000.6.7f1 is verified, and only on the platforms listed on the Unity SDK page; test other editors and platforms yourself before shipping.

Docs: [Unity SDK](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/sdk/unity.html), [Plugin bindings](https://open-play.b4klabs.dev/docs/en/plugins/bindings.html).

## Do

- Look up docs through MCP first; link the page you used in the PR description.
- Keep Open Play calls in one module/service layer, one writer per feature (never write the same state both locally and through Open Play).
- Handle every SDK session state, including `reauthRequired`, `banned` and `logoutUncertain`.
- Add a test with each integration change; report failing checks, never skip them.

## Don't

- Do not guess endpoints, headers, field names or error codes.
- Do not put a server key, token or cookie in client code, tests, logs or commits.
- Do not use `latest` or git/vendored copies of the SDK; do not hand-copy DTOs.
- Do not bypass CSRF, `Origin` or idempotency checks "just for testing".
- Do not remove a domain, redirect URI or environment that a live host still uses.
- Do not store save data in browser storage alone once the player can sign in.
- Do not write retry loops without backoff, or retry non-idempotent calls with new keys.
- Do not run production deploys or destructive operations unless the user explicitly asks.
````

Next step: [Quickstart](quickstart.md) and the [Production checklist](../operations/production-checklist.md).

docs.description: Defines the concepts of studio, game, environment, module, API key types, player session, and plugin.
docs.body:
# Core concepts

Everything in Open Play revolves around a few concepts: the **environment** that data belongs to, the **modules** that turn features on and off, two kinds of **API key**, the player's **session**, and the **plugin** that carries game-specific logic. Read this page once; the other pages assume you know these words.

## Studio, game, environment

Open Play uses a three-level hierarchy. In the panel you manage this tree on the **Studios and games** screen (visible only to the super admin).

| Level | Meaning | Note |
|---|---|---|
| **Studio** | The organization that holds your games together | A server can have more than one studio |
| **Game** | A single product | When a new game is created, the `dev` and `prod` environments are opened automatically |
| **Environment** | An isolated copy of the game: `dev`, `prod`, and `staging` if you want it | Players, characters, wallets, and keys belong to an environment |

**The environment is the data boundary.** A player, character, wallet, or key in one environment is not visible from another environment. Every API call runs against a single environment:

- In calls made **with an API key**, the environment comes from the key; you do not send an extra header.
- In calls made **with a player session**, you declare the environment with the `x-crx-env: <environment-id>` header. The ID is a UUID. The SDKs send it from the `environmentId` setting.

> [!NOTE]
> Today the panel does not show the environment ID (UUID) in a readable field. Ask your operator team for the ID, or read it from the `environmentId` field in the response to the `GET /v1/panel/modules` request that the **Game settings › Modules** tab makes in a panel session. This gap is on record.

For the panel steps, see [Quickstart](quickstart.md#1-create-a-game-and-an-environment) and [Game settings](../panel/game-settings-environments.md).

## Modules

Most features are modules: `characters`, `economy`, `items`, `trading`, `store`, `rewards`, `social`, `chat`, `competition`, `notifications`, `webhooks`, `scenes`, `plugins` (13 modules). Modules are turned on and off **per environment**; at installation the wizard has you choose a starter set, and afterwards you use the **Game settings › Modules** tab (super admin only).

- The endpoints of a disabled module do not work: HTTP `404` with the body `{"code":"module_disabled","message":"…","module":"<name>"}`. A caller with invalid credentials gets `401` and cannot find out that the module is disabled.
- Disabling does not delete data, it only stops the surface; when you enable it again the data is still there.
- Some modules depend on others (for example `trading` relies on `economy` and `items`), and a module that an active plugin needs cannot be disabled.
- Core surfaces (player sign-in, content groups, API keys) are not modules and cannot be disabled.

For error details, see [Errors](../reference/errors.md).

## API keys: server and client

An API key is a secret string bound to an **environment**, sent with the `Authorization: Bearer` header. Its format:

```text
crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
```

The panel shows only the `crx_live_<prefix>` part (the prefix); the secret is shown **once, at the moment it is created** and cannot be recovered. If you lose it, you create a new key or rotate the key: the old secret becomes invalid and the new one is shown once.

| | Server key | Client key |
|---|---|---|
| Where is it used? | Your game server, your backend code | The game client (browser, mobile) |
| Can it be embedded? | **No**, keep it secret | Yes |
| What can it do? | All operations: creating definitions, granting money, minting items, registering webhooks, administration | Only permitted, non-sensitive operations |
| Example | the `add_xp` command, granting money, minting items | reading a character, the `set_flag` command |

The exact rule changes **per endpoint** and is tested per endpoint in code. Which endpoint accepts which key type is listed in the [endpoint reference](../reference/endpoints.md). If the key type is insufficient, the call gets `403`.

To create a key in the panel: **Game settings › API keys › New API key** (see [API keys](../panel/game-settings-api-keys.md)). When you create one, you enter a name, the type (Server key or Client key), the validity period, and a note written to the audit log (optional; at most 500 characters).

> [!WARNING]
> **Advanced settings** (scope labels, permissions, extra information) are for record-keeping only today; they do not restrict what the key can access. Only the key type determines access. Do not treat a server key as "restricted".

For managing keys and secret values, see [Security](../operations/security.md).

## Player session

Players talk to the server not with an API key but with their own **sessions**. A session is opened in these ways: guest sign-in, email and password, Google. On a successful sign-in the server writes a session cookie (`__Secure-crx.session`) and a refresh cookie (`__Secure-crx.refresh`); the same tokens are also returned in the response body, so clients without cookies (the Unity native build, command-line tools) can use `Authorization: Bearer <session-token>`.

Every request made with a player session carries the `x-crx-env` header. In a cookie-based (browser) session, state-changing requests additionally require **CSRF** protection (the `x-csrf-token` header). The SDKs manage these details for you; with raw REST you implement them yourself:

- [Authentication overview](../auth/overview.md)
- [Sessions and CSRF](../auth/sessions-and-csrf.md)

The player session can also be carried to **your game server**: the player's short-lived **access JWT** (EdDSA) is verified offline with a shared JWKS. See [Server-side verification](../auth/server-verification.md).

## Plugin

A plugin is a package **compiled into the server** that carries game-specific server logic (commands, queries, realtime modules). Plugin calls are made under `/v1/plugins/{plugin}/...`; state-changing commands carry an idempotency key and, if the schema requires it, a version check with `expectedVersion`. A plugin's schema is an artifact (`<plugin>.plugin.schema.json`), and the TypeScript/Unity bindings are generated from this schema.

> [!NOTE]
> Loading third-party plugins (from the panel or the API) is not supported today. Plugins come with the Open Play server release. See [Plugins overview](../plugins/overview.md).

## Common call rules

The same three rules apply to many endpoints; you will find the details in the reference pages:

- **Idempotency-Key:** for state-changing commands, the same key and the same body replay the result; the same key with a different body returns `422`. See [Idempotency and concurrency](../reference/idempotency-and-concurrency.md).
- **If-Match / expectedVersion:** by declaring the version of the resource that you read, you catch a concurrent write conflict (`409`).
- **Numbers:** large integers (`i64`) become `bigint` in JavaScript; in the plugin protocol they are carried as decimal strings. See [Numbers and encoding](../reference/numbers-and-encoding.md).

For short definitions of terms, see the [Glossary](../reference/glossary.md).

# Game rules and automations

This page describes the two parts of the panel's "Rules" screen: the **game rule values** that the game's plugin reports (for example police thresholds) and the **automations** that do work automatically when an event happens. Read it if you want to tune the game's behavior without shipping code or react automatically to an event.

## What it does

- **Game rule values:** The game's plugin reports which numbers are adjustable (name, unit, lower and upper bound, step, default). An operator changes these values in the panel and **publishes** them; the new values take effect in the game shortly (in about 6 seconds at the latest). Every publish becomes a new version and you can return to old values with one click.
- **Automations:** Rules of the form "when this event happens, if this condition is true, do this". A rule attaches to character events (`level_up`, `xp_added` …) and gives the character a stat, resource, flag, modifier or reward. Conditions are written as a CEL expression; in the panel a structured builder generates the CEL for you.

Game rule values are a panel surface: your game server does **not** write them with a REST endpoint; the plugin reads the values on the server. Automations are managed both from the panel and with REST (they are part of the `characters` module).

## Where it lives in the panel

| What you want to do | Panel page |
|---|---|
| An overview of the Rules screen, topics and cards | [Rules](../panel/rules.md) |
| Edit, publish and preview a game rule card | [Rule card](../panel/rules-game-card.md) |
| See the publish history and the diff, roll back | [Rule history](../panel/rules-history.md) |
| Create, edit, enable and disable an automation | [Automation editor](../panel/rules-automation-editor.md) |

> [!NOTE]
> Panel help pages are not translated yet; the panel links above point to the Turkish source, and the panel itself is shown in Turkish.

## Game rule values

### Model

- **Catalog:** Reported by the game's plugin. There are topics, cards and each card's parameters; every parameter comes with a unit (for example seconds, meters, percent) and bounds. If there is no catalog or the plugin does not report one, only Automations appear in the panel.
- **Version:** The effective values are the latest version. If there has been no publish, the plugin's code defaults are used ("Kod varsayılanı", the code default). Publishing and rolling back write a new version; history is not deleted.
- **Apply time:** If a parameter is `canlı` (live), it is applied shortly after the publish; if it is `yeniden başlatmada` (on restart), the old value stays until the game server restarts, and the panel shows both together as "Yayında / Bekliyor" (Published / Pending).
- **Validation:** Values are validated on the server against the catalog bounds, step and cross-field constraints; an invalid field is reported per field. The plugin re-validates with the same bounds; an invalid value does not break the game, and the plugin falls back to its code defaults.
- **Permission:** Reading is open to the four panel roles; publishing and rolling back only to the `super_admin` and `game_manager` roles. Publishing and rolling back accept an optional justification (at most 500 characters) and are written to the audit log.
- **Concurrency:** A publish carries the version you saw (`expectedVersion`); if someone else published while you were looking, `409` is returned and you need to refresh the tab.
- **Preview:** The panel runs a scenario (for example a continuous speed violation) with the plugin's real logic using today's and the proposed values and shows the event timeline; it saves nothing.
- **Client warning:** If a parameter is `clientVisible`, the game client reads it from the plugin's query. If the client does not read that value yet, the panel warns you while publishing.

### Effect on the game

Your game code does not read game rule values with REST. The plugin takes the values from a single snapshot at every step on the server; the values the client needs come through the plugin's own query. This behavior is plugin-specific; today only the `package-ride` plugin reports a catalog. Third-party plugins reporting a catalog and being loaded is **not supported yet**; see [Plugins: overview](../plugins/overview.md).

## Automations

### Model

- **Rule:** `key` (a unique key), `trigger_type` (the trigger event), `condition` (a CEL expression), `actions` (a list of actions) and `priority`. A rule is versioned; every publish is a new version.
- **Trigger:** `flag_set`, `attribute_set`, `resource_changed`, `modifier_added`, `modifiers_removed`, `xp_added`, `level_up`, `ability_unlocked`, `event_emitted`, `character_rolled_back`. An unknown type is rejected. The panel builder does not offer the `character_rolled_back` option.
- **Actions:** `add_stat` (`key`, `delta`), `add_resource` (`key`, `delta`), `set_flag` (`key`, `value`), `add_modifier`, `remove_modifier` and `grant_reward` (`what`: a fixed amount of money `{ "type": "currency", "key", "amount" }` or a reward table `{ "type": "table", "key" }`).
- **CEL context:** The condition has the variables `character`, `event`, `now` and `seed`; the functions `has_ability`, `base_stat` and `clamp` can be used. The context carries time and seed, a rule cannot read its own clock; there is no `now()` or `random()`. Rules are compiled at registration, not at run time.
- **Budget (fixed):** In one command chain at most 50 rules are evaluated and 200 actions are produced, the chain depth cannot exceed 5, and a condition expression cannot exceed 500 nodes. Exceeding it is **fail-closed**: the command is rejected with `429` and which limit was exceeded is stated. Two rules that trigger each other are cut off by this limit.

### Panel builder

The builder produces CEL from a "When → Conditions → Do" structure: condition rows (field, operator, value) are combined with **all** (`&&`) or **any** (`||`); at most 20 conditions and 10 actions can be added. Text values are escaped; line breaks and control characters are rejected. When the builder is used, the server recompiles the rule (the CEL text the client sends is not read for a builder rule). A new rule starts **disabled**; the "enable right away" option is unchecked. Before publishing you can do a **dry run** with a sample event; it is not required.

### Calls your game makes

Rule endpoints are called with an **API key**:

```
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
```

| Method and path | What it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/rules` | Saves a rule (`201`) |
| `GET /v1/rules` | Lists rules (`cursor`, `limit`) |
| `GET /v1/rules/{key}` | Reads the rule's current version |
| `POST /v1/rules/{key}/enable`, `POST /v1/rules/{key}/disable` | Enables / disables the rule (`204`) |
| `DELETE /v1/rules/{key}` | Deletes the rule (`204`) |
| `POST /v1/rules/dry-run` | Tries a rule against a character without writing |

> [!WARNING]
> **Key gate:** The endpoints that write rules (save, delete, enable/disable) and `POST /v1/rules/dry-run` work only with a **server key**; a client key gets `403`. The rule read endpoints (`GET`) still accept a client key.

The TypeScript SDK exposes these endpoints in a typed way: `createRule`, `listRules`, `getRule`, `deleteRule`, `enableRule`, `disableRule`, `dryRunRule` (see [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md)). These endpoints take raw CEL text; the panel builder's structured model exists only on the panel surface.

#### Saving a rule

```
POST /v1/rules
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "key": "lvl10_reward",
  "trigger_type": "level_up",
  "condition": "event.to == 10",
  "actions": [
    { "type": "grant_reward", "what": { "type": "currency", "key": "gold", "amount": 1000 } },
    { "type": "set_flag", "key": "reached_level_10", "value": true }
  ],
  "priority": 0
}
```

```json
{ "key": "lvl10_reward", "current_version": 1, "enabled": true, "created_at": "2026-11-03T09:00:00Z" }
```

A rule saved with REST starts **enabled right away** (`enabled: true`); unlike the panel builder, to start it disabled call `POST /v1/rules/{key}/disable` after saving. `event.to` is the new level of the level-up event; event fields vary by trigger. The registration is rejected if the condition cannot be compiled, the trigger is unknown or a budget limit is exceeded.

#### Dry run

```
POST /v1/rules/dry-run
Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "condition": "character.progression.level >= 10", "actions": [ { "type": "set_flag", "key": "veteran", "value": true } ], "character_id": "0192f0f2-…" }
```

```json
{ "condition_result": true, "node_cost": 7, "would_produce_events": [ { "...": "…" } ], "would_grant": [], "warnings": [] }
```

A dry run writes no events and grants no rewards.

## Versioning and replay safety

- Publishing and rolling back game rules: done by the panel with `Idempotency-Key` and `expectedVersion`; the same key returns the same version again and writes a single audit record.
- Automation publishing: every publish is a new version; old versions are not deleted, and "roll back" rewrites the old version as a new version.
- The REST rule endpoints have no `Idempotency-Key` or `If-Match`.

## Events

The actions a rule runs produce normal character events (`flag_set`, `xp_added` …); these can be delivered through [webhooks](webhooks.md). A reward produced by a rule also produces the `reward_granted` event.

## Limits

- In a command chain: 50 rules, 200 actions, depth 5, 500 nodes per condition.
- In the panel builder: at most 20 conditions and 10 actions.
- A game rule justification is optional; at most 500 characters.
- Game rule integer values are limited to ±(2^53−1) in the panel.

## Common errors

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `429` (command) | The rule chain exceeded the budget | Simplify the rules that trigger each other |
| `400`/`422` on registration | The CEL could not be compiled, unknown trigger or field | Try the condition with a dry run first |
| `409` in the panel (publish) | Someone else published while you were looking | Refresh the tab and publish again |
| Field error in the panel (`422`) | The value is outside the bound, step or constraint | Respect the bound the field shows |
| I published the value but the game behaves the old way | The parameter is applied `yeniden başlatmada` (on restart), or the 6 seconds have not passed | Look at the panel's "Bekliyor" (Pending) indicator |

## Working example

The two requests above (the `lvl10_reward` registration and the dry run) together form a complete flow: first try the condition with a dry run, then save it with `POST /v1/rules`, then make a character level up with an `add_xp` command and verify that the rule ran, following the flow on the [Characters](characters.md) page.

## Related pages

- [Characters](characters.md) · [Rewards](rewards.md) · [Webhooks](webhooks.md) · [Notifications](notifications.md)
- [Plugins: overview](../plugins/overview.md) · [TypeScript SDK](../sdk/typescript.md)

docs.body:
# Security

This page gathers what you need to know to operate a game integrated with Open Play securely: where to keep keys, how to rotate them, how the browser session is protected, and how to verify webhook requests. Read it together with the [production checklist](production-checklist.md) before going to production.

## 1. API keys

There are two key types, and both are bound to a single **environment**:

| Type | Where it is kept | What it can do |
|---|---|---|
| **Server key** (`server`) | Only on your server (a secret manager or an environment variable) | All server endpoints |
| **Client key** (`client`) | Can be embedded in the client | Sensitive commands (for example `add_xp`, `set_attribute`) do not work; but some endpoints have no key-type gate ([endpoints](../reference/endpoints.md)) |

> [!WARNING]
> **A client key is scoped to the environment, not to the player.** Character creation/deletion, inventory movements, trading, merchant buy-sell, trying rules, using VIP cards and wallet transfers work only with a **server key**; a client key gets `403`. However, most read endpoints (`GET /v1/characters`, `/v1/wallets`, `/v1/items`, `/v1/inventories/{owner}` …) still accept a client key, and a key embedded in the game can read any player's data in the environment. For a player's own items, own trading and own character, use the endpoints that work with a player session (`/v1/player/...`, plugins, `PlayerClient`); the owner always comes from the session.

### Key format and storage

- Format: `crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>`. The server stores only the key's **digest** (argon2id); it cannot regenerate the secret part.
- The secret value is shown **only once, at creation time**. If you lose it, it cannot be recovered; you generate a new key.
- Do not put the key in the repository, logs, error reports, the client bundle, or screenshots. Filter the `Authorization` header out of logs.
- Use a **separate key per environment and per service** (for example the live API server, a batch job, an admin script); in a leak you revoke only one.
- Give the key an **expiry date**. `expiresAt` can be set when creating it in the panel; an expired key is rejected.

### Lifecycle

Keys are managed in the panel on the **Game settings: API keys** screen ([API keys](../panel/game-settings-api-keys.md)):

| Action | Effect |
|---|---|
| Create | A new key; the secret value is shown once |
| Disable / enable | Temporary and reversible |
| Rotate | Creates a new key with the same name and **immediately revokes the old one in the same operation** |
| Revoke | Permanent; cannot be undone |
| Delete | Soft delete + revoke |

The key state is **re-read from the database on every request**: a revoke or disable takes effect on the next request (only the verification result of the secret value is cached for 60 s, the state is not). A reason is written for every operation and it goes into the [operation history](../panel/audit.md).

### Rotation without downtime

The **Rotate** action in the panel revokes the old key immediately; until you roll out the new key, your calls get `401`. To rotate without downtime:

1. In the panel, create a second key **with a different name** (there can be only one active key with the same name and owner at a time).
2. Write the new key into your secret manager and roll it out by restarting your services.
3. Verify that no service uses the old key (the operation history and your own logs).
4. **Revoke** the old key.

### If a leak happens

1. **Revoke** the leaked key immediately (the effect is on the next request).
2. Roll out the new key in the order above.
3. In the operation history and your own logs, look for unexpected operations after the moment of the leak (wallet transfers, item minting, webhook registration).
4. In the environments the key could access, review the webhook endpoints; an attacker may have registered an endpoint (registered secrets are shown once, but a new registration generates a new secret).

## 2. Player session and browser security

- After player sign-in the server writes three cookies: `__Secure-crx.session` (session), `__Secure-crx.refresh` (refresh), and `__Secure-crx.csrf` (CSRF). All three carry `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `Path=/`, and `SameSite=Lax` (scripts cannot read them); the plain value of the CSRF token given to the script is not in the cookie but in the response header and body. The `__Secure-` prefix **requires HTTPS**: a session cannot be established over plain HTTP.
- The session **slides for 30 days**: it is extended if the player makes a request at least once a day. **The absolute ceiling is 180 days**: no matter how active, a new sign-in is needed after 180 days. An open realtime socket does not keep the session alive. The durations are fixed in server code.
- The environment can turn on a **single active session** rule if it wants (a new sign-in drops the old one); this is among the sign-in settings in the panel.
- The access JWT (EdDSA) is not the session token; your game server verifies it offline with `GET /v1/auth/jwks` ([server verification](../auth/server-verification.md)).

### CSRF

In a cookie session, every modifying (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) request passes two protections:

1. **Origin check:** the host in the `Origin` (or `Referer`) header must be one of the environment's allowed origins. A host bound to an environment can target only that environment. It is blocked if `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` and `Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate` are together. Clients that send no `Origin` at all (curl, server-to-server) pass this check; the layer that protects them is double submit.
2. **Double submit:** the `__Secure-crx.csrf` cookie and the `x-csrf-token` header must arrive together and match. The token is **single-use** and rotates on every successful verification: store the new `Set-Cookie` and `x-csrf-token` value in the response for the next request. `GET /v1/auth/csrf` for a new token.

The TypeScript SDK manages this automatically; if you write HTTP by hand, see the [sessions and CSRF](../auth/sessions-and-csrf.md) page. The failure case: `403` and the plain text `permission denied`.

### CORS and same origin

The server sends CORS headers **only to `https://<domain>` origins in the environment domain list** (and the operator's global allowed list), and only on the public API: the allowed origin is reflected verbatim, `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` is added, `*` is never used, and the panel path (`/v1/panel/*`) never gets CORS. **CORS is not authorization:** `Origin`, the CSRF double submit, and the environment checks run unchanged; CORS only lets the browser read the response. Do not add extra CORS headers to your own proxy: duplicate headers cause a browser error.

Because the session cookie is `SameSite=Lax`, a direct call works only if the game and Open Play are on the **same site** (subdomains of the same registrable domain); on a different site, use a reverse proxy. Topology: [architecture and hosting](../getting-started/architecture-and-hosting.md#calling-from-the-browser-direct-cors-or-reverse-proxy).

The allowed origins are **your environment domains**. The domain you define for the environment in the panel is the basis both for routing to that environment and for the `Origin` check ([Game settings: environments](../panel/game-settings-environments.md)). A modifying request from an unknown host is rejected.

## 3. Webhook verification

Open Play sends the events you subscribe to your endpoint with a signed `POST`. **You must verify every request**; do not process an unsigned request.

| Header | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `X-Crx-Signature` | `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>` |
| `X-Crx-Event-Id` | The event ID (UUID); the deduplication key |
| `X-Crx-Event-Type` | The event type ([webhook events](../reference/webhook-events.md)) |

The signature: `HMAC-SHA256(secret, "{t}.{raw body}")`, lowercase hexadecimal. The key is the `whsec_…` text you received at registration itself (as bytes). Rules:

1. Sign/verify the **raw body**: if you decode the JSON and rewrite it, the bytes change and the signature does not match.
2. Use a **constant-time** comparison (`timingSafeEqual`, `hmac.compare_digest`).
3. Compare the `t` value with your own clock and reject anything outside the window (5 minutes is recommended; this is a receiver policy, the server does not enforce it).
4. **At-least-once:** the same event may arrive more than once. Deduplicate with `X-Crx-Event-Id` and make the operation replay-safe.
5. Only a `2xx` response is success. Respond quickly (queue the work); other statuses are retried.

Delivery behavior:

| Behavior | Value |
|---|---|
| Retry | Exponential backoff: starts at 1 s, grows by powers of 2, capped at 5 minutes, ±20% jitter |
| Maximum attempts | 10; after that the delivery becomes `failed` (dead-letter queue, DLQ) |
| Redirect | Not followed |
| Body limit | A body above 64 KiB is not sent |
| Endpoint address | `https` only; private, loopback, and link-local IP addresses and addresses containing user info (`user:password@`) are rejected at registration (SSRF protection) |
| Secret key | Returned in the registration response **only once**; rotation = deleting the endpoint and registering it again |

> [!NOTE]
> There is no in-place "rotate" for the webhook secret. For a seamless transition: register the new endpoint (with the new secret), have your receiver verify both, and delete the old endpoint.

Verification example (Node, `node:crypto`):

<!-- snippet: examples/ts/security-webhook-verify.ts -->
```ts
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

/** İmzalı webhook isteğinin doğrulama sonucu. */
export type WebhookCheck = { ok: true; eventId: string; eventType: string } | { ok: false; reason: string };

const TOLERANCE_SECONDS = 300; // yeniden oynatma penceresi: alıcı politikasıdır, 5 dakika önerilir

/**
 * Open Play webhook isteğini doğrular. `rawBody`, ayrıştırılmamış HAM bayt dizisi olmalıdır:
 * JSON'u çözüp yeniden yazarsanız imza tutmaz.
 * İmza: HMAC-SHA256(secret, "{t}.{ham gövde}"), başlık biçimi `t=<unix saniye>,v1=<hex>`.
 */
export function verifyWebhook(
  secret: string,
  rawBody: Buffer,
  headers: { signature: string | undefined; eventId: string | undefined; eventType: string | undefined },
  nowSeconds: number = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
): WebhookCheck {
  const parts = Object.fromEntries((headers.signature ?? "").split(",").map((part) => part.trim().split("=", 2) as [string, string]));
  const timestamp = Number(parts["t"]);
  const received = parts["v1"];
  if (!Number.isInteger(timestamp) || received === undefined) return { ok: false, reason: "imza başlığı bozuk" };
  if (Math.abs(nowSeconds - timestamp) > TOLERANCE_SECONDS) return { ok: false, reason: "zaman damgası pencere dışında" };
  const expected = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${timestamp}.`).update(rawBody).digest("hex");
  const a = Buffer.from(expected, "utf8");
  const b = Buffer.from(received, "utf8");
  if (a.length !== b.length || !timingSafeEqual(a, b)) return { ok: false, reason: "imza uyuşmuyor" };
  if (headers.eventId === undefined || headers.eventType === undefined) return { ok: false, reason: "olay başlıkları eksik" };
  return { ok: true, eventId: headers.eventId, eventType: headers.eventType };
}
```

Monitor delivery status and the DLQ in the panel: [Webhooks and event queue](../panel/webhooks.md). For registration and endpoint management, see the [webhooks guide](../guides/webhooks.md).

## 4. Rotating secrets: summary

| Secret | How it is rotated |
|---|---|
| Server/client API key | Create a second key, roll it out, revoke the old one (above) |
| Webhook secret | Register a new endpoint, update the receiver to accept both, delete the old one |
| Player password | The player changes their own password (all sessions drop) or the password reset flow ([email and password](../auth/email-password.md)) |
| Player sessions | The user signs out; an admin revokes the player's sessions (panel or `POST /v1/auth/admin/revoke-player-sessions`) |

## 5. What not to write to logs

The API key, session and refresh tokens, the CSRF token, the realtime ticket, the webhook secret, OAuth `state` and `code` values, passwords, and the guest secret value. The SDKs do not include these in error objects; in your own logging code, too, do not print the request raw.

## 6. Other notes

- **Error detail is not leaked:** the server gives no internal detail in a `500` response; account existence is also not leaked (a wrong password and an unknown address get the same response).
- **Banned account:** on sign-in endpoints, `403 account_banned` after ownership has been proven; no distinction is made on other endpoints ([errors](../reference/errors.md)).
- **Safety switches:** in the panel you can loosen or force back some protection rules per environment; every change is recorded with a reason ([Safety switches](../panel/safety-switches.md)).
- **Plugins** are trusted code compiled into the server; running third-party plugins and isolation do not exist yet ([plugins](../plugins/overview.md)).
- **Panel admin accounts** have a separate identity line and two-factor authentication; there is no two-factor authentication for player accounts.

# Player characters

## Purpose

This page lists the characters in the selected environment. A character is the entity a player plays in the game; its state (level, attributes, resources) changes through commands, and every change is recorded. Use it to find a character, open its profile and, if needed, create a new character by hand. Character templates (definitions) are not on this page; they are on the Content page.

## When to use

- To check the state of a player's character.
- To filter characters of a given type, such as drivers.
- To create a character by hand for testing or support.

> [!NOTE]
> If the characters module is disabled, this page does not appear in the menu. Enable the module on the [Game settings › Modules](game-settings-modules.md) page.

## Step by step

### Finding a character

1. Make sure you selected the right game and environment; the list shows only the selected environment.
2. Narrow by type with the **Tümü** (All), **Sürücüler** (Drivers) and **Diğer** (Other) buttons at the top.
3. Use the table's search box and filter menu to narrow by name, type, level or date.
4. Click the row to open the profile. For the profile page, see [Character profile](character-profile.md).

### Creating a new character

1. Press **Yeni karakter** (New character). Only admins with permission to create characters see this button.
2. Choose the character's type from the **Tanım** (Definition) list. If there is no definition, first publish one on the Content page.
3. If you like, write the ID from your game server in the **Dış kimlik** (External ID) field.
4. Write an **İşlem nedeni** (Action reason) and press **Oluştur** (Create). The character is created immediately and you are taken to its profile.

## Fields and options

### New character form

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Tanım (Definition), or Tanım anahtarı (Definition key) | Yes | The definition the character is created from; its current version is used |
| Dış kimlik (External ID) | No | An ID to match your game server; a second character cannot be created with the same ID |
| İşlem nedeni (Action reason) | No | The reason written to the audit log; optional, at most 500 characters |

### Columns in the list

The columns Oyuncu (Player), Tür (Type), Seviye (Level), Puan (Score), Teslimat (Deliveries), Son değişiklik (Last change) and Oluşturulma (Created) are shown by default. You can turn on the Dış kimlik (External ID) and Oyuncu kimliği (Player ID) columns from the column menu. Old placeholder driver records that have no player carry a "Taşınmamış" (Not migrated) badge.

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| The list looks empty | Check that you selected the right environment and that no filters are active. |
| It says "Bu ortamda henüz tanım yok" (There is no definition in this environment yet) | A character is created from a definition. Publish a definition on the Content page and come back. |
| "Bu anahtarla yayınlanmış bir tanım yok" error (There is no published definition with this key) | The definition key is wrong or the definition is not published. Pick it from the list or publish the definition. |
| "Bu dış kimlikle zaten bir karakter var" error (A character with this external ID already exists) | Enter another external ID or leave the field empty. |
| The "Yeni karakter" button is missing | Your account's role cannot create characters; ask an admin. |

## Related docs

- [Characters](../guides/characters.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)
- [Authentication overview](../auth/overview.md)

# API keys

## Purpose

API keys let your game's server prove its identity to Open Play. This page lists the keys of the selected game and environment, and lets you create new keys and manage their expiry and status. It is the **API anahtarları** (API keys) tab inside **Oyun ayarları** (Game settings).

## When to use

- When you connect your game server to Open Play for the first time.
- To revoke a key that has leaked or is no longer needed.
- To extend a key's expiry or rename it.

## Step by step

### Creating a new key

1. Use the environment selector at the top to choose the game and environment the key will work in.
2. Press **Anahtar oluştur** (Create key). Only admins with key write permission see this button.
3. Give the key a name and choose the **Anahtar türü** (Key type): **Sunucu anahtarı** (Server key) for your game server, **İstemci anahtarı** (Client key) for the game client.
4. Pick a period under **Geçerlilik** (Validity). If you are unsure, a period such as 90 days that you renew regularly is safer.
5. Write a short reason in the **Not** (Note) field.
6. Press **Anahtarı oluştur** (Create the key).
7. Copy the secret value shown on the page right away and store it somewhere safe.
8. The same card shows the **Ortam kimliği (environmentId)** (Environment ID) below the secret value. Use this value when you set up the SDK; the button next to it copies it.

> [!WARNING]
> The secret value is shown only once, when the key is created; it cannot be viewed afterwards. If you lose it, you must rotate the key.

### Using the key

Your game server sends the key in the `Authorization` header with every request:

```bash
curl https://<your-server>/v1/<endpoint> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer crx_live_<prefix>_<secret>"
```

Replace the placeholders with your own values. Do not write the real key into source code or the game client.

### Environment ID for the SDK

The SDK asks for the environment's ID (`environmentId`) when you set up the player client: `createPlayerClient({ baseUrl, environmentId })` in TypeScript, `OpenPlayUnity.Options(...)` in Unity. A key only works in the environment it was created in; the panel shows that environment's ID in two places:

- When you create or rotate the key, on the one-time card below the secret value.
- Always, on the key's detail page in the **Kimlik ve sahiplik** (Identity and ownership) card.

The environment ID is not secret; it can go into the game client. The value is shown in full; copy it as it is with the **Ortam kimliğini kopyala** (Copy environment ID) button.

### Editing, rotating and revoking a key

1. Click the key's row in the list to open its detail page.
2. Use **Düzenle** (Edit) to change the name, expiry and notes; the secret value does not change.
3. **Rotate** revokes the old secret and shows the new value once.
4. **Devre dışı bırak** (Disable) pauses the key temporarily, **Etkinleştir** (Enable) turns it back on; **Revoke** is permanent.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Anahtar adı (Key name) | Yes | A name to recognise the key in the list; at least 2 characters |
| Anahtar türü (Key type) | Yes | Server (secret) or client (can be embedded in the game) |
| Geçerlilik (Validity) | Yes | No expiry, 30 days, 90 days, 1 year or a custom date; when editing there is also "Değiştirme" (Do not change) |
| Not (Note) | No | The reason written to the audit log; optional, at most 500 characters |
| Anahtarın sahibi (Key owner) | No | Default is "Bu ortam" (This environment); it is under "Gelişmiş ayarlar" (Advanced settings) |
| Sahip oyuncu / organizasyon (Owner player / organization) | Depends on the owner type | Required once you pick an owner |
| Kapsam etiketleri (Scope labels) | No | Labels for notes only |
| İzinler (Permissions) | No | Name-value notes; they do not restrict access |
| Ek bilgiler (Extra information) | No | Name-value notes; they do not restrict access |

> [!NOTE]
> Scope labels, permissions and extra information are for your records only for now. What a key can access is decided by the **key type** (server or client).

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| I lost the secret value | Rotate the key with **Rotate**; save the new value and update it on your server. |
| A key stopped working one day | It may have expired, been disabled or been revoked; check its status and end date on the detail page. |
| The "Anahtar oluştur" button is missing | Your role has no key write permission; ask an admin. |
| The SDK asks for `environmentId`; where do I find it? | Copy it from the **Ortam kimliği (environmentId)** (Environment ID) row on the key's detail page. The value is also shown on the card where you created the key. |
| A server key was embedded in the client | Revoke the key immediately, create a new one and use it only on the server. |

## Related docs

- [Quickstart](../getting-started/quickstart.md)
- [Server-side verification](../auth/server-verification.md)
- [Security](../operations/security.md)

# Environments and domains

## Purpose

A game can have several **environments**: development (dev), staging and live (prod). Each environment has its own players, data and API keys. This tab lists the game's environments as cards; it lets you bind each environment to its own domains, add a new environment and archive an environment. The tab is open only to a super admin.

## When to use

- To bind a new address to an environment when your game will be opened from it in a browser.
- To add a staging or development environment.
- To hide an environment that is not used.

## Step by step

### Bind a domain

1. In the **Alan adları** (Domains) box on the environment's card, write one domain per line (for example `oyun.example.com`). Names are lowercased; empty lines and duplicates are dropped.
2. Write your reason in the **Gerekçe** (Reason) field.
3. Press **Alan adlarını kaydet** (Save domains).

### Add an environment

1. Press **Ortam ekle** (Add environment) at the top of the tab.
2. Choose the environment kind: Development (dev), Staging or Live (prod). The window selects Staging by default.
3. Write your reason and confirm. Domains and Google sign-in are bound separately after the environment is added.

### Archive or reopen an environment

The **Arşivle** (Archive) button under the card hides the environment; no data is deleted. An archived environment shows a **Geri aç** (Reopen) button and its domain fields are disabled.

> [!WARNING]
> Keep the old address in the list until the new address works and the old one redirects. Once an address is removed, a game opened from it cannot sign in or write records at once. When you press Save, the removed addresses are listed in a dialog; the change is not applied until you choose **Yine de kaldır ve kaydet** (the confirm button). If the list becomes empty, the server's general allowlist applies.

> [!NOTE]
> Domains are used as an allowlist in the origin check of requests coming from a browser. Bind every address you serve your game from to the right environment; a domain bound to another environment is not accepted.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Domains | No | One domain per line; at most 10 |
| Reason | No | Optional; at most 500 characters |
| Environment kind (add window) | Yes | Development, Staging or Live |
| Action reason (in windows) | No | Optional; at most 500 characters |

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Bu alan adı başka bir ortama bağlı" (This domain is bound to another environment) | The same domain cannot be bound to two environments. Remove it from the other environment first. |
| "En fazla 10 alan adı bağlanabilir" (At most 10 domains can be bound) | Shorten the list; at most 10 domains can be bound to one environment. |
| "Önce başka bir ortam seçin" (First select another environment) | The currently selected environment cannot be archived; select another environment from the top bar. |
| The tab says "permission required" | This tab is open only to a super admin. |
| The game on the old address cannot sign in | The address was removed from the list. Add it back and save, then finish moving to the new address. |
| Archiving was rejected | The environment has a live grant or an active API key; the window shows the reason. |

## Related docs

- [Architecture and hosting](../getting-started/architecture-and-hosting.md)
- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)

docs.body:
# Studio settings

## Purpose

This page provides studio owners and administrators with centralized control over studio configuration, games, panel and API addresses, domain names, and integrations. From here, you can rename the studio, manage the studio's games and environments (create new games, archive, delete permanently), copy its immutable slug and fixed access URLs, configure custom domain names, connect your Cloudflare account for automated DNS management, inspect active product modules, and navigate to the studio members screen. Platform-level operations such as provisioning studio storage, suspending or reactivating the studio, and support-based access ("Enter panel") are managed from the central platform panel.

## When to use

- To update the display name of your studio.
- To add a new game to your studio, rename existing games, archive or unarchive them, or open game settings.
- To permanently delete a game and its database data.
- To copy the studio panel address (`https://<domain>/` once a domain is added, otherwise `https://<host>/s/<slug>/panel/`) or player API address (`https://<domain>/api` on the studio's own domain, `https://<host>/api/<slug>` on any host) for sharing with teammates or configuring game clients.
- To connect a custom domain (for example `panel.yourcompany.com`), verify DNS records, or designate a primary domain.
- To link your studio's Cloudflare account ("Cloudflare connect") for automated DNS record creation.
- To inspect which product modules are enabled for the studio.
- To open the Studio members page to manage team invitations and roles.

## Step by step

### General information and addresses

1. **Studio name**: Click **Rename** to update the studio name (1-160 characters), provide an optional reason, and save.
2. **Slug (short name)**: The studio slug is read-only; it is globally unique and cannot be modified after creation.
3. **Panel address**: The canonical studio panel address. Without a connected domain it is the permanent path (`https://<host>/s/<slug>/panel/`); with an active primary domain (custom domain or subdomain) the panel lives at the root of that domain (`https://<domain>/`) and older links that open the permanent path (bookmarks, emails) redirect to the domain on load. Use the adjacent copy button to copy it to your clipboard.
4. **Player API address**: The base URL where game clients and SDKs connect. With the studio's own domain it is `https://<domain>/api` (for example `https://lantern-tide.open-play.tech/api`, endpoints under `/api/v1/...`), otherwise the permanent path `https://<host>/api/<slug>`; both reach the same studio. Use the copy button to copy it. Realtime WebSocket connections connect to `/v1/realtime/ws` under this address.

### Games

This section is visible to studio owners and administrators.

> Your studio's games. A new game is provisioned with development and production environments; archiving only hides, deletion is permanent.

1. **Games list**: Displays the studio's own games, each with its development (dev) and production (prod) environments.
2. **New game**: Click **New game** to provide a game name (1-160 characters) and an optional short name (slug; up to 48 characters, automatically derived from the name if left blank). Each new game is provisioned with development and production environments, and its data lives in its own area inside the studio's database. The game switcher in the panel header reflects the new game immediately.
3. **Per-game actions**: Each game row provides the following actions:
   - **Rename**: Updates the display name of the game.
   - **Archive / Unarchive**: Hides the game from the switcher and active lists, or restores it. Archiving does not delete any data.
   - **Game settings**: Navigates to the game's general settings screen.
   - **Delete**: Opens the permanent deletion dialog to remove the game and its database data.
4. **Permanently delete game**:
   - The **Delete** action opens the "Permanently delete game: <name>" dialog. The dialog states: *"The game and its data in the studio database are permanently deleted. This cannot be undone."*
   - To confirm, you must type the game's exact short name (slug) into the confirmation box. Until the slug matches exactly, the **Delete game permanently** button remains disabled.
   - A two-factor authentication (2FA) verification code is requested only if the operator's account has 2FA enabled; users without 2FA are not prompted for a code.
   - Entering a reason is optional.
   - The game does not have to be archived first; active games can be deleted directly.
5. **Switching upon deletion**: If the currently selected game is deleted, the panel automatically switches to another available game in the studio or displays the empty state.

### Managing domains

To access the studio panel through your own domain name:

1. **Add custom domain**: Click **Add custom domain**. If your Cloudflare account is connected, use **Pick from a domain in my Cloudflare account**: choose the domain from your account (there can be one or several) and type the subdomain (if left empty, the domain itself is added); the resulting address is shown below and Open Play writes the DNS record (CNAME to the platform's target, proxy off). If your DNS is at another provider, use **At another DNS provider** and type your domain name yourself (for example `panel.yourcompany.com`). The domain starts in **Pending** status.
2. **DNS and verification**:
   - If Cloudflare is connected: the CNAME record is written automatically to the zone in the studio's Cloudflare account (the verification TXT records too in Cloudflare edge mode). The moment you connect the account, the records of your pending domains are written right away. If your zone already has the same CNAME, the row shows **Existing record used**; that record is not deleted when you close the domain. If the zone is not in the account, the row states the reason and you add the record manually.
   - Manual (the same at every DNS provider): at your DNS provider, create a **CNAME** record for your domain pointing to the target the platform gives you (proxy off, "DNS only"; the target is shown on the row with a copy button). Open Play serves the verification file (`/.well-known/open-play-verify`) itself and the platform obtains the certificate; you do not upload any file.
   - In both cases Open Play checks the verification file itself (the certificate is ready in about 1-2 minutes) and the domain becomes **Active** on its own; the **Verify** button is for trying right away and does not fail the domain if it is not ready. If it cannot be verified within 15 minutes, the row becomes **Failed**: fix the record and press **Retry**.
3. **Set primary**: Click **Set primary** on an active domain to designate it as the default panel address. A primary domain cannot be disabled.

### Cloudflare connect

Link your studio's Cloudflare account to automate DNS records for custom domains:

1. Click **Connect with Cloudflare**.
2. Enter an optional reason and click **Go to Cloudflare**.
3. In the Cloudflare authorization window, select your account and grant DNS write and zone read permissions.
4. Once connected, the card lists the domains in your account. Click **Add here** next to the domain you want the panel on, type the subdomain (for example `panel`) and add it: Open Play writes the CNAME record and the domain becomes active on its own once the certificate arrives.
5. When authorized, you are redirected back to the canonical studio panel address: `https://<domain>/#/studio` if you started from the domain (not the permanent `/s/<slug>/panel/` path), or `https://<host>/s/<slug>/panel/#/studio` if you started from the permanent path. The status updates to **Connected**.
6. To disconnect, click **Disconnect**. DNS records for active domains remain in place to avoid disruption; records for closed domains are cleaned up.

### Modules and members

- **Modules**: Displays which product modules are enabled within the platform ceiling. Modules disabled by platform operators cannot be enabled from the studio panel.
- **Studio members**: Click the **Studio members** link to manage team member invitations, roles, and open sessions.

## Fields and options

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Studio name | Yes | 1-160 characters; the studio's display name |
| Slug | No | Read-only; immutable identifier used in paths |
| Panel address | No | Read-only; copyable studio panel URL |
| Player API address | No | Read-only; base URL for SDKs and clients |
| Game name | Yes | 1-160 characters; the game's display name in panel and switcher |
| Game slug | No | Up to 48 characters; lowercase letters, digits, hyphens (generated if blank) |
| Confirm slug | Yes | Exact short name (slug) match required to enable deletion |
| Verification code (TOTP) | No* | *Only requested when operator has 2FA enabled; numeric one-time-code |
| Custom domain | Yes | The domain to add (at least two labels) |
| Reason | No | Optional explanation (up to 500 characters) |

## Common situations

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| Cannot edit the slug | The slug determines permanent paths and is globally unique; it cannot be modified after creation. |
| "This game's data is not in the studio database yet; it cannot be deleted" error | The game's data still resides in the platform's shared database (older games). Such games cannot be deleted until they are migrated to the studio database; contact the platform team. |
| "A move is in progress; try again when it finishes" error | A data placement or migration job is currently in progress; wait for it to complete and try again. |
| Domain stays in "Pending" or "Failed" status | DNS propagation may take several minutes. Make sure the CNAME record points to the target the platform gave you and that the proxy (for example Cloudflare's orange cloud) is off; Open Play checks by itself for 15 minutes, press **Verify** to try right away or **Retry** after the 15 minutes have passed. If the row shows an "Add manually" reason, add the record yourself at your DNS provider. |
| Cloudflare authorization error | Ensure all requested zone read and DNS write permissions were granted on Cloudflare; reinitiate connection if needed. |
| A module is locked and cannot be turned on | The module is restricted by the platform operator ceiling; contact platform support to request access. |
| Cannot see studio home or suspension controls | Studio home provisioning, suspension, and platform support impersonation are managed exclusively from the central platform panel. |

## Related docs

- [Core concepts](../getting-started/concepts.md)
- [Architecture and hosting](../getting-started/architecture-and-hosting.md)
